q.intro.text: You are cutting floor tiles. Each tile must be an exact copy of the template ABC. You may trace the template, then slide, turn or flip the tracing paper.

q.ask.text: Which tile can the tracing cover exactly, corner on corner?

e.intro.text: Four steps. Press each one: the picture moves first, then the board writes it down.

e.s1.text: Match the corners by their sides. A sits at the right angle, between the four-unit side and the three-unit side. So does D. So A goes with D, B with E, and C with F.

e.s2.text: A, B, C goes counterclockwise, but D, E, F goes clockwise. Only a flip reverses that, so flip the tracing over the y-axis. A prime lands at six, two.

e.s3.text: A prime is at six, two and D is at six, negative four, straight below it: slide six down.

e.s4.text: Check every corner: A double prime is on D, B double prime on E, C double prime on F. The tracing covers the tile exactly, so triangle ABC is congruent to triangle DEF.

e.why.text: Quick check: why does this prove the tiles are congruent?

e.w-ok.text: Yes. The tracing only moved; it never stretched. And every corner landed on its partner.

e.w-look.text: Looking alike is not a proof: tile one looked alike too. The tracing has to land exactly, on every corner.

e.w-one.text: One corner is not enough. B and C have to land on E and F too.

t.intro.text: Your turn: show that triangle ABC is congruent to triangle DEF. Matching the corners and the first move are done for you.

t.match.text: A goes with D, B with E, C with F. Both go counterclockwise, so no flip is needed.

t.turn.text: First move: turn ninety degrees counterclockwise about the origin. A prime lands at negative one, one.

t.slide-ask.text: Now the slide. It starts at A prime negative one, one and ends at D one, negative four. Fill in its rule.

t.slide-ok.text: Yes: from A prime negative one, one to D one, negative four is two right and five down.

t.slide-orig.text: That slide goes from A to D. But the turn already moved A: the slide starts at A prime negative one, one.

t.slide-back.text: That goes from D back to A prime. Count from A prime to D: across, then down.

t.slide-other.text: Count from A prime negative one, one to D one, negative four: across first, then down.

t.check-ask.text: The tracing has landed. Which check proves triangle ABC is congruent to triangle DEF?

t.k-ok.text: Right: every corner is on its partner. triangle ABC is congruent to triangle DEF.

t.k-one.text: A double prime on D is a start, but the other corners have to be checked too.

t.k-two.text: Two corners are not enough: the mirror image of the triangle fits them too. Check C double prime as well.

t.cb-right.text: You were right: tile two. Turned and flipped copies are congruent, as long as the tracing covers them exactly.

t.cb-one.text: Tile one looked like the template, but its long side is five units, not four. Tile two is the congruent one, even though it is flipped.

t.cb-both.text: Tile one only looks alike: its long side is five units, not four. Only tile two is congruent.

t.cb-none.text: Tile two is the congruent tile: a flip and a slide cover it exactly.

p.intro.text: Jordan has two rectangles: P is six by two and Q is four by three. Jordan says: “Both cover twelve squares, so they are congruent.”

p.build.text: Now prove it. Fill each “because” with the reason that makes the line true.

p.build-test.text: Let’s test it. Fill each “because” with the reason that makes the line true, and see where it leads.

p.claim1.text: A slide, turn or flip keeps every side length,

p.claim2.text: P has a side of six, and Q has no side of six,

p.claim3.text: So no sequence of moves puts P exactly on Q,

p.c1.text: Right. Watch the tracing: it turns and slides, and its sides stay six and two.

p.c2.text: P’s sides are six, two, six and two. Q’s sides are four, three, four and three. The six has no partner.

p.c3.text: Put the tracing on Q any way you like: the six-unit side always sticks out.

p.x-area.text: Equal areas don’t make figures congruent: six by two and four by three both make twelve.

p.x-try.text: One move that fails proves nothing: maybe another one works. The side lengths are the proof.

p.x-other.text: True, but it is the reason for a different line. Which reason makes this line true?

p.done.text: That’s a proof: three claims, each with its reason. P and Q have the same area, but they are not congruent.
